title: When Kaira's Milk Farmers Refused Polson and Built Their Own Dairy
dek: In January 1946 Gujarat dairy farmers cut off their only big buyer, and Tribhuvandas Patel was asked to organise them into a co-operative of their own.

story.company: Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union (later Amul)
story.event: Organising Kaira's dairy farmers against the Polson dairy and founding their own co-operative
story.summary: In the mid-1940s milk producers in Kaira district, Gujarat, sold through middlemen to Polson, a private dairy at Anand that supplied Bombay; refused even a modest increase, they stopped supplying it. After a farmers' meeting on 4 January 1946 called by Morarji Desai on Vallabhbhai Patel's advice, Tribhuvandas Patel was asked to organise them, and the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union was founded that year. It began operating in 1948 with two village societies; Verghese Kurien, posted to Anand's government creamery in 1949, stayed to help, and by 1962 the union had 219 societies and 46,400 members.
paragraphs: On 4 January 1946, milk producers met in the village of Samarkha in Kaira district, Gujarat. Morarji Desai had called the meeting on the advice of Vallabhbhai Patel, and their grievance was one buyer. Polson, a private dairy set up at Anand in 1929, bought their milk through middlemen and sent it to Bombay, mainly to the city's milk scheme, at a handsome profit. One later account says traders refused to buy when milk was plentiful and called it poor when it was scarce. When the farmers asked for a share of the profits, Verghese Kurien later wrote, they were refused even a modest increase.

Their answer was to stop selling and build a buyer of their own. The farmers went on strike, refusing Polson their milk. Vallabhbhai Patel gave Tribhuvandas Patel, a local freedom fighter and follower of Gandhi, the task of "making the Kaira farmers happy and organize them into a cooperative unit." The Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union was founded that year. Membership was open to any producer, and each member had one vote, however many buffaloes they kept.

It began small. In 1948 the union started operating with two village societies and a small dairy handling about 500 pounds of milk a day, according to the citation for a 1963 Ramon Magsaysay Award. The Bombay government agreed to take its whole supply of pasteurised milk at stable, premium prices. In May 1949 a young engineer, Verghese Kurien, was posted to the government creamery at Anand to serve out a bond. He found the job dull and, by his own account, volunteered to help Tribhuvandas Patel set up a processing plant. He stayed.

By 1962 the union had 219 village societies with 46,400 members, the milk it processed that year was worth more than $6 million, and its products were sold as Amul. When Tribhuvandas Patel retired as chairman in the early 1970s, members gave him a purse of 600,000 rupees, one rupee from each, and he used it to start a foundation for the health of women and children in Kheda district.

quote.text: It is hard to leave the world (to become a friar), it is hard to enjoy the world; hard is the monastery, painful are the houses; painful it is to dwell with equals (to share everything in common)
quote.source_title: Dhammapada, a Collection of Verses, tr. F. Max Müller, Project Gutenberg eBook #2017
quote.connection: The Dhammapada does not pretend that living as equals is easy; it lists it among life's pains. The Kaira union asked farmers with one buffalo and farmers with many to pour into the same cans and hold one vote each. That it lasted does not mean it was painless.

reflection: Each Kaira farmer had a litre or two to sell and no way to bargain alone. What changed their position was not a better argument with Polson but a different arrangement: a buyer they owned, with a vote each. Tribhuvandas Patel's job was less to fight than to keep people together long enough for that arrangement to work.

When you feel stuck with a single employer, supplier or customer who sets the terms, it may help to ask who else is stuck in the same place, and what you could build together that none of you could build alone.
invitation: Name one person who faces the same problem you do in your work. Send them a short message today asking how they handle it, with no plan beyond listening to the answer.

cross_checks.claim: Polson, a private dairy at Anand, bought Kaira's milk through middlemen, and the farmers organised against it.
Vallabhbhai Patel set the effort going and Tribhuvandas Patel was given the task of organising the farmers.
The Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union was founded in 1946.
The union started with only two village societies.
Kurien was posted to the government creamery at Anand on a bond and stayed to work with the union from 1949.

research_notes: Founding date: the union was registered in 1946 (Indian Cooperative, BusinessLine, Wikipedia gives 14 December 1946; the Magsaysay citation's header also says 1946), but the 1963 Magsaysay citation's text says it was 'organized in 1948' from two village societies, and Amul marked its 25th anniversary in 1973. The story says it was founded in 1946 and began operating in 1948. Meeting place: Kurien's 2004 paper names Samarkha village on 4 January 1946; Wikipedia (citing a Tehelka article that is no longer online) names a meeting at Chaklasi; the story follows Kurien. The widely repeated length of the milk strike (often given as 15 days) and the first-day collection of about 250 litres were not found in a source that loads, so neither is given; the Magsaysay figure of about 500 pounds a day is used instead, attributed to the citation. Kurien's arrival: his own paper says he was posted to the Anand creamery in May 1949; The Hindu's op-ed says he returned to India in 1948 and was sent to Anand; Indian Cooperative says Tribhuvandas Patel hired him in 1950; The Hindu's news report says he joined in 1949. The story uses Kurien's May 1949 posting. The 1962 figures (219 societies, 46,400 members, over US$6 million) come from the 1963 Magsaysay citation only and are attributed to that year. The phrase 'making the Kaira farmers happy and organize them into a cooperative unit' is Kurien's quotation of Sardar Patel's instruction and is kept with its original wording. The one-member-one-vote rule is from BusinessLine's description of the Kaira co-operative model. Funding is mixed: farmer-owned shares, a state milk contract and, later, government, UNICEF and New Zealand help for the processing plant (Magsaysay citation). The World Bank PDF loads but its text is not extracted by the verifier, so it shows as live without a name match. The Dhammapada verse is about monastic and household life; it is applied here by analogy.
